title: Full-Time RV Insurance: What Full-Timer Coverage Adds, and Why a Vacation RV Policy Isn't Enough When the RV Is Home
description: Living in your RV? Full-timer coverage adds home-style liability and medical payments a vacation RV policy lacks. What it covers, domicile issues and gaps.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: A standard RV policy assumes you have a fixed home; full-timer coverage fills the liability and medical payments gap a homeowners policy would normally cover.
Full-timer liability applies to many incidents away from the RV, not only around the vehicle.
Your premium and legal minimums are set by your domicile state, not where you happen to be parked.
Not telling the insurer the RV is your only home can put claims at risk.
Pair full-timer coverage with replacement-cost or agreed-value physical damage and strong personal effects limits.

faqs.question: What is full-timer RV insurance?
faqs.answer: Coverage added to an RV policy for people who live in their RV, providing personal liability and medical payments similar to a homeowners policy.

faqs.question: Do I need full-timer coverage if I live in my RV part of the year?
faqs.answer: Insurers usually define full-time use by whether the RV is your primary residence. If you still own a home with homeowners insurance, you may not need it; ask the insurer for its definition.

faqs.question: Which state's insurance rules apply to full-time RVers?
faqs.answer: Generally your domicile state, where the RV is registered and you hold your license, though you must also meet the minimums of states you drive through.

faqs.question: Is full-time RV insurance expensive?
faqs.answer: It adds cost over a vacation policy, but it replaces liability protection you would otherwise lose when you sell your home. See [California RV insurance](/learn/california-rv-insurance/) for typical cost drivers.

content.text: Selling the house and living on the road changes your insurance more than most new full-timers expect. The homeowners policy that quietly covered your liability, your belongings and guest injuries is gone, and a vacation-use RV policy wasn't designed to replace it. This spoke builds on our [California RV insurance guide](/learn/california-rv-insurance/) and the broader [state auto insurance compliance guide](/learn/state-auto-insurance-compliance-guide/).
Vacation RV Policy vs Full-Timer Coverage

rows: Broader personal liability, similar to homeowners
Liability away from the RV (e.g., your dog bites someone at a park)
Higher limits available; essential when everything you own is aboard
Designed for RV as primary residence

content.title: Disclose Full-Time Use
content.text: If you tell the insurer the RV is a weekend vehicle but you live in it, a large liability or contents claim can be investigated as a misrepresentation. Tell the insurer it is your primary residence and buy the right coverage.
Your Domicile State Sets the Rules

Full-timers still need a legal domicile for registration, licensing and insurance. Many choose states known for full-timer services, including Florida. If your domicile is Florida, the legal minimum is PIP and property damage liability, not bodily injury, which is far too thin for a heavy motorhome; see [Florida minimum car insurance requirements](/qa/florida-minimum-car-insurance-requirements/). If you register in California, the motorhome needs 30/60/15 and you must show proof on demand; see [California evidence of liability insurance](/learn/california-evidence-of-liability-insurance/).

items: **High auto liability limits**, plus an [umbrella policy](/learn/umbrella-insurance-guide/) if you have savings to protect.
**Replacement-cost or agreed-value physical damage** so a total loss doesn't pay a depreciated [actual cash value](/glossary/actual-cash-value/).
**Personal effects** at a limit that matches everything you own.
**Emergency expense** for lodging when the RV is in the shop; you have no other home to go to.
**Coverage for anything you tow.** A trailer or car behind the motorhome has its own gaps; see [does car insurance cover a travel trailer](/qa/does-car-insurance-cover-travel-trailer/).

content.title: Run a Gap Check Before You Sell the House
content.text: Before cancelling your homeowners policy, list every risk it covered and confirm each one is handled by the new RV policy. Our [8-Point Policy Check](/policy-check/) is a quick way to do it.

Your domicile also affects [health insurance](/insurance/health-insurance/) networks, vehicle inspections and jury duty, so choose it deliberately. Insurance-wise, the key is consistency: the address on your license, registration and policy should match your declared domicile.
